- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if history shows volatility.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated mid-to-late horizon values; apply dampening factor to peaks.
- Forecasting horizon 1–7 days: model tends to be overly optimistic; adjust downward by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Forecasting horizon 8–30 days: model often fails to capture mean reversion; if sentiment is mixed or declining, reduce forecast slope toward historical mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 spikes followed by 0.00/0.33 drops, model overreacts; apply lagged correction: subtract 15–30% from forecast 3–5 days after spike.
- Model underperforms in low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.33) — especially when true values are near zero — avoid extrapolating from recent highs; use floor at 0.5–1.0 unless sentiment rebounds.
